title: Sholazar Basin
body: Sholazar Basin is a hidden jungle in the northwest of Northrend, ringed by mountains, where the frozen continent gives way to steaming rivers, mangrove swamps and warm rain. Great crystal pillars rise around its edges, works of the titans, and the gorlocs called the Oracles tend stone shrines they believe the Great Ones left for them, while the wolvar of the Frenzyheart, newcomers to the basin, mean to take it. In the east the Scourge has broken in, and a towering guardian holds the line.

title: Nesingwary Base Camp
body: On a river in the west of the basin, Hemet Nesingwary's expedition has made its base camp after a hard landing: its ship ran aground and its flying machine came through too damaged to send reports home. An archmage of Dalaran helped fund it in return for samples of the basin's plants and crystals. The Venture Company, digging at the foot of a crystal pillar, shoots down its supply flights and harasses its scouts.

parts.body: The bones of a beast the gorlocs revere warned the hunter to leave this land in peace once he had his prize, for he does not belong here. No dead rhino, he answered, tells Hemet Nesingwary what he can hunt.

title: Frenzyheart Hill
body: Frenzyheart Hill is the home of the Frenzyheart Tribe, wolvar who came to Sholazar not long ago looking for a new home. High-Shaman Rakjak rules here, and he means for his people to take the basin: the gorlocs, whom the wolvar call big-tongues, must leave or be killed. The tribe can be vicious, an elder admits, but they are good people, friends with the smart and the strong; they just do not like the dumb.

parts.body: In the southwest the Frenzyheart call a great beast, Kartak, to a feast of big-tongues with oracle blood, and if a hunter is worthy, Kartak takes that hunter's body and lends its rage to the slaughter.

title: Rainspeaker Canopy
body: Rainspeaker Canopy is a gorloc village in the boughs of an enormous tree, the heart of the Oracles. Its people keep the Great Rain Stone, which they believe was left by the Great Ones who made them, and care for it with offerings of shinies dug from the earth; in return, they say, it takes care of them. High-Oracle Soo-say wants peace, and every offering he has sent the wolvar has been answered with threats.

parts.body: Soo-holu is the protector the Great Ones left at the shrines long ago, who wakes only when they are disturbed, and lets those it trusts share its body to turn its power on the wolvar.

title: The Crystal Pillars
body: Great pillars of crystal rise around the edges of the basin, works of the titans that the gorlocs hold sacred. Four still stand. The fifth, the Lifeblood Pillar, lies broken, its largest piece resting where it fell with a cave in its side, and the Scourge walks among its scattered red crystal; up the ridge the gorloc village of Mosswalker is a village of the dead.

parts.body: The titans set five pillars around the basin, pouring out pure lifeforce, and while all five stood the Scourge could never have broken in.
sources: quest 12736 description (Glimmering, Suntouched, Mosslight and Skyreach Pillars; Lifeblood Pillar broken, other pillars still good)

parts.body: No undead could come near the pillar while it stood, so it was the living who brought it down: the Cult of the Damned, with powder kegs, opening the breach for the dead.

parts.body: In the fallen shard waited the lich Artruis, holding a wolvar and a gorloc as pawns to force their hero to choose a side. The pillar's crystals weakened him, and he fell.

title: The Blight Line
body: Beyond the Rainspeaker Rapids the green of Sholazar ends at the Blight Line, and past it lie the Lost Lands, sick and grey, where the Scourge's blight spreaders poison the ground. In the east the jungle vanishes under a great slide of snow and ice, the Avalanche, where the Scourge has the run of the land in its hundreds. Along the line the servants of Freya stand against the dead.

parts.body: In these lands, where the power of life rules, the Avatar warns, all harm the Lich King's agents inflict will be returned to them sevenfold.
sources: quest 12803 description (the Blight Line between Rainspeaker Rapids and the Lost Lands)

parts.body: Into the Avalanche the Avatar unleashed the Etymidian, a colossus of the titans that tore through the Scourge host and its masters.

title: Avatar of Freya
body: The Avatar of Freya is a towering guardian who walks the Rainspeaker Rapids, where the green of the basin meets the blight; the expedition's professor speaks of a lifewarden the titans appointed to look over Sholazar, and she fits the description. The Scourge are a blemish on her pristine lands, she has sworn by the might of her creators to crush them, and she trusts no outsider who will not fight them.

parts.body: She is the embodiment of a single aspect of Freya, daughter of the titans, left as the Lifewarden. She never imagined the Lich King would send willing living servants to do his work.

title: The Makers' Perch and the Waygate
body: Three works of the titans keep their silence at the edges of the basin. The Makers' Perch stands on the western rim and the Makers' Overlook high in the eastern mountains, halls of titan stone where stone guardians still keep watch. At the southern end of the basin stands the third, a titan waygate, dark for seven centuries.

parts.body: Woken by switches in the two halls, the waygate opened on a distant land, where a colossus of stone stood with engravings that left no doubt: this was the Etymidian, the weapon the Avatar had spoken of.
